samples.summary: Slides text-body style validation is stricter than the slides reader, so a GET → edit → PUT round-trip of an existing deck can now 400
samples.evidence: `assertValidTextBodyBlocks` calls `assertValidBlockStyle` (line 602), which throws on any present style value that is not a finite number (`value !== undefined && (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value))`, controller line 329-336) — so `lineHeight: null`, `marginTop: null`, or an alignment outside `BLOCK_ALIGNMENTS` is a 400. Unlike the docs arm, slide text bodies are persisted and returned VERBATIM (`writeSlidesRoot`/`readSlidesRoot` store plain JSON; the comment at line 570-576 states this explicitly and deliberately relaxes only the *structural* checks). Consequently a deck already holding such a value is readable through GET but no longer writable through PUT — the CLI read-modify-write flow breaks on data the caller never touched. The docs arm avoids this because `parseBlockStyleAttrs` drops the same values on read; the slides arm has no such normalizer. Either normalize on the slides read path or make the slides style check drop-and-continue instead of throwing.

samples.summary: Group children are now validated with the full `assertValidElement`, which can reject decks that previously round-tripped
samples.evidence: `assertValidElement` now recurses into `data.children` (line 550-555) and applies the full element contract — non-empty `id` (line 509) and an object `frame` (line 519) — to nested elements that were never validated before. Group children are persisted verbatim as JSON with no reader-side normalization, so any legacy/imported group child missing `id` or `frame` turns a previously-accepted PUT into a 400, breaking GET → edit → PUT for that deck. The docs arm sidesteps this only because `readDocsRoot` synthesizes the fields it demands; nothing does that for slides.

samples.summary: `tableData.rowHeights` is still unvalidated and a non-array value crashes the writer with a 500 — the exact failure class the new checks exist to remove
samples.evidence: `buildBlockNode` does `if (block.tableData.rowHeights && block.tableData.rowHeights.length > 0) { ...rowHeights.map(...) }` (docs-tree.ts:224-227). A PUT body with `tableData: { columnWidths: [], rows: [], rowHeights: 'abc' }` passes every check in `assertValidBlock` (which validates only `columnWidths`, `rows`, cells, cell `style` and inlines) and then throws `TypeError: rowHeights.map is not a function` inside `doc.update` → HTTP 500 instead of a 400. The diff added sibling guards (cell.style, inline.text/style) for exactly this reason but left this dereference uncovered.
searchedFor: grep for rowHeights in the controller

samples.summary: `removeNodeStyle`'s `[from, from+1)` range may still include the node's first child, and no test covers a shared attribute name on that child
samples.evidence: `tree.removeStyle(from, from + 1, attrsToRemove)` relies on Yorkie excluding a node whose opening tag sits exactly at `from + 1` (the first child). The new tests only assert survival of attributes on *grand*children (the inline at depth 2 in 'should not strip backgroundColor from nodes inside the cell', and the nested cell in the colSpan test) — the first child of a cell is a block node, which happens to carry none of the removed attribute names, so a one-off inclusion would be invisible today and would silently strip attributes the moment a child node type shares a name (e.g. a future block-level `backgroundColor`). Worth verifying the SDK's range semantics or asserting on the first child directly.

samples.summary: A cleared ('') list-marker color no longer falls through to the inline's color, unlike every other 'cleared means unset' path in this change
samples.evidence: `const colorSource = m?.color ?? firstInline?.color;` — `??` treats the empty string as *present*, so a marker whose color was cleared to '' shadows the inline color and `resolveStoredColor` then maps it to `theme.defaultColor` (the new test at render-list-marker.test.ts asserts exactly this). Everywhere else in this diff '' is defined to mean 'unset'; here 'unset' should fall through to `firstInline?.color`, matching the pre-existing comment the diff replaced. The old comment justified `??` on the premise that no falsy value was legal — this change invalidates that premise without updating the operator.

samples.summary: `toRgbHexColor` treats an empty alpha component as fully transparent and drops the color
samples.evidence: The regex's optional alpha group is `(?:,([^)]*))?`, so `rgb(1,2,3,)` / `rgba(0,0,0, )` yield `rgb[4] === ''` (or whitespace). `isTransparentAlpha` then computes `Number('') === 0`, which is finite and `<= 0`, and the whole color is dropped as transparent. A trailing-comma/empty alpha is malformed CSS, but the documented intent ('anything unparseable is treated as opaque, so a color the user can see is never dropped') is inverted for this input. Guard with a non-empty check before `Number()`.

samples.summary: New unbounded recursion in the PUT validator (group children, nested text-body tables) has no depth limit
samples.evidence: `assertValidElement` recurses through `data.children` (line 552-554) and `assertValidTextBodyBlocks` recurses through `tableData.rows[].cells[]` (line 616) with no depth budget. A deeply nested but otherwise well-formed body produces a `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` inside the request handler, i.e. a 500 from the very validator whose stated job is to turn malformed payloads into 400s.

samples.summary: `parseMarginFromEdgeAttr('')` returns 0 where the previous reader returned the default
samples.evidence: Old backend code was `attrs.marginFromEdge ? Number(attrs.marginFromEdge) : DEFAULT_HEADER_MARGIN_FROM_EDGE`, so an empty-string attribute fell back to 48. The new helper only special-cases `undefined`; `Number('')` is 0 and finite, so an empty attribute now yields a 0 px header offset. No current writer emits '', so this is latent, but the read guard is advertised as covering hand-edited/legacy CRDT attributes and does not cover this one.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. assertValidBlockStyle (docs-content.controller.ts:314-338) throws a 400 for any present style value that is not a finite number (null included, since `value !== undefined` passes and `typeof null === 'object'`) and for any alignment outside BLOCK_ALIGNMENTS (crdt-attrs.ts:23-38). assertValidTextBodyBlocks reaches it for slide text bodies (controller:596-606), including recursively for table cells (616-619) and via assertValidElement for text/shape/table/group (532-555). The slides read path is verbatim: readSlidesRoot (yorkie/slides-tree.ts:52-81) only unwrapJson's the stored arrays with no style normalization, and GET returns it directly (controller:119-123); writeSlidesRoot (slides-tree.ts:93-110) stores plain JSON. The docs arm is genuinely asymmetric because parseBlockStyleAttrs (docs/src/model/crdt-attrs.ts:86-98) drops non-finite numbers and unknown alignments on read — its own comment (76-84) says this preserves GET→PUT identity — while the slides arm has no such normalizer, and the slides validator comment (controller:567-577) relaxes only structural checks. I found no guard or caller-side sanitizer making the path unreachable, so a deck already holding such a value is readable via GET but 400s on PUT of untouched data: a real read-modify-write correctness break.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is present exactly as described: docs-content.controller.ts:550-555 recurses into `data.children` with the full `assertValidElement`, which mandates a non-empty string `id` (:509-513) and an object `frame` (:519-523), throwing BadRequestException otherwise. The premise that slides content is stored/returned verbatim also checks out: readSlidesRoot (yorkie/slides-tree.ts:52-81) only unwraps JSON and writeSlidesRoot (:93-110) assigns arrays as-is, with no id/frame backfill; the frontend's migrateElement (packages/slides/src/model/migrate.ts:155-168) likewise synthesizes neither. The controller's own comment at :567-577 acknowledges this exact regression class for verbatim-persisted slide data (strict field requirements would 400 a GET→edit→PUT of a legacy deck) yet the element walk applies the strict contract at every depth. Counter-evidence exists but is not conclusive: children are typed Element[] with required id/frame (packages/slides/src/model/element.ts:251-255, :402), all in-repo producers set both (import/pptx/shape.ts:236-258, store/memory.ts:1087-1119), and consumers dereference ch.frame unconditionally (model/group.ts:221, 301), so such data would already break the editor. That makes the impact doubtful but does not make it impossible for previously-accepted (unvalidated) nested children written through this same PUT endpoint to now be rejected. No guard elsewhere blocks the path, and the issue is in the correctness lane, so I cannot refute on a named ground.
